section_summary: This section records 1947 correspondence about American patent rights in occupied Japan, including royalty claims, alleged copies of Parker pens, and requests for Japanese patent records. A Civil Property Custodian report then surveys patent, trademark, and copyright holdings, wartime seizures, royalties, proposed policies, and Japanese law, with organizational orders and memoranda in its appendix.

subfiles.title: Patent interests of Northern Equipment Company in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards records and reports on Northern Equipment Company's Japanese licensee and royalties.
subfiles.summary: Reports wartime royalty deposits, destruction of the Gadelius factory, and a proposed subcontracting arrangement in Kobe.

subfiles.title: Northern Equipment Company request for claim information
subfiles.from: E. W. Scarlett, Northern Equipment Company
subfiles.about: Requests an answer about Japanese assets and filing a claim with the Alien Property Custodian.
subfiles.summary: Says the company has waited a year for information and wishes to protect its claim.

subfiles.title: Reply to Northern Equipment Company on patent interests
subfiles.from: Francis B. Flaherty, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: E. W. Scarlett, Northern Equipment Company
subfiles.about: Sends records and explains findings about Gadelius royalties, its destroyed factory, and proposed production.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Political Adviser's materials and describes Gadelius's wartime operations, royalty deposits, and planned subcontracting with Ishida Valve Company.

subfiles.title: Commerce request concerning Parker Pen patents
subfiles.from: A. D. O'Keefe, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Chief, Civil Affairs Division, War Department
subfiles.about: Requests transmission to SCAP of a memorandum about Japanese copies of American fountain pens.
subfiles.summary: Urges SCAP to be informed of alleged patent infringement and forwards a proposed memorandum.

subfiles.title: Proposed memorandum for SCAP on Parker pen imitation
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Describes Parker's objection to a Japanese pen resembling its Vacumatic model.
subfiles.summary: Parker says the sample copies its pen and arrow clip and asks that manufacture stop.

subfiles.title: War Department forwarding letter on Parker patents
subfiles.from: R. H. Chard, War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: O. J. McDiarmid, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce's letter and proposed SCAP message on Parker patent infringement.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the June 9 letter and its proposed message after a conversation between the offices.

subfiles.title: Reply to Arthur Middleton on Japanese patents
subfiles.from: Edwin H. Martin, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains pending patent-restoration policy and current controls on exports that infringe Allied patents.
subfiles.summary: Says restoration policy is under discussion and cites a required Japanese certification that exports do not infringe Allied intellectual property.

subfiles.title: Reference slip forwarding Middleton correspondence
subfiles.from: Charles H. Mitchell
subfiles.about: Routes attached correspondence for attention following a telephone conversation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards attachments for appropriate attention.

subfiles.title: War Department transmittal of Middleton letters
subfiles.from: R. H. Chard, War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: Division of Foreign Service Administration, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Middleton's letters about Japanese and Philippine patents for a reply.
subfiles.summary: The Civil Affairs Division lacks the information to answer and refers Middleton to the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Arthur Middleton inquiry on Japanese patents
subfiles.from: Arthur Middleton
subfiles.about: Asks how a client can recover Japanese patents seized during the war.
subfiles.summary: Reports apparatus offered for sale in Japan that allegedly falls under the client's former patents.

subfiles.title: Arthur Middleton inquiry on Philippine patents
subfiles.from: Arthur Middleton
subfiles.about: Asks whether United States patents can still be extended to the independent Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Seeks the current procedure following Philippine independence.

subfiles.title: Questions on Japanese-held United States patents
subfiles.from: Philip G. Strong, Acquisition and Distribution Division
subfiles.about: Requests lists and information concerning Japanese nationals' United States patents and claims.
subfiles.summary: The surviving page asks about patents, applications, government measures, publications, and claims.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese Patent No. 172865
subfiles.from: H. Wickliffe Rose, American Viscose Corporation
subfiles.about: Requests a copy of a postwar Japanese rayon-fiber patent and clarification of patent policy.
subfiles.summary: Rose explains that SCAP has withheld patent copies pending Washington policy and asks for instructions releasing this patent.

subfiles.title: Reply to Rose on Japanese Patent No. 172865
subfiles.from: Raymond Vernon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Declines a special release while patent policy awaits consideration by the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Suggests Rose obtain the copy when normal Japanese patent operations and private communications resume.

subfiles.title: Parker Pen complaint forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo, for the Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Forwards Parker's complaint about Japanese copies of its fountain pens.
subfiles.summary: Quotes Ivan D. Tefft's April 1 letter alleging weak protection for foreign patents and widespread imitation of Parker pens. Requests whatever action SCAP considers appropriate.

subfiles.title: Transmission of study on American patent claims
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sends a study of patents issued by Japan to United States nationals for SCAP's Patent Property Division.
subfiles.summary: Notes that detailed information on infringement claims is unavailable and forwards four copies of the study.

subfiles.title: Westinghouse inquiry on Japanese patents and royalties
subfiles.from: R. H. Wood, Westinghouse Air Brake Company
subfiles.about: Asks for a property-restoration release and advice on recovering Japanese patents and blocked royalties.
subfiles.summary: Seeks the official announcement and asks whether an agent with power of attorney can recover the company's interests.

subfiles.title: Reply to Westinghouse on patents and royalties
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains procedures for releasing royalties and the pending policy for restoring patent rights.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Press Release No. 532. Says an authorized agent may seek royalty release, while patent recovery awaits policy and Japanese records.

subfiles.title: Reply to Schering on patent applications in Japan
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains that applications from outside Japan are not yet being received.
subfiles.summary: Says policy on restitution and new applications awaits Far Eastern Commission action.

subfiles.title: Political Adviser despatch on Parker infringement
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Parker's complaint and SCAP's response concerning Japanese pen imitations.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the Civil Property Custodian replied directly to Parker and encloses the correspondence.

subfiles.title: Parker Pen formal complaint to SCAP
subfiles.from: Ivan D. Tefft, Parker Pen Company
subfiles.to: Patent Property Division, Civil Property Custodian, SCAP
subfiles.about: Complains formally about Japanese pens simulating Parker's Vacumatic and '51' models.
subfiles.summary: Describes earlier export-market litigation and identifies Nakata Co., Ltd. as maker of a recent imitation. Requests action against production.

subfiles.title: SCAP response to Parker Pen Company
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.to: Parker Pen Company, attention Ivan D. Tefft
subfiles.about: Explains protection for Allied patent property existing in Japan on December 7, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Says Japanese authorities are investigating infringement, but current directives do not cover property never legally established in Japan.

subfiles.title: Request to transfer Japanese patent copies
subfiles.from: United States Army Forces, Middle Pacific, to Joint Chiefs of Staff; forwarded to State
subfiles.to: Department of State, for Martin and Jones
subfiles.about: Requests authority to send Japanese patent volumes to the United States Bureau of Patents.
subfiles.summary: Says copies from 1923–1945 are urgently needed for examination under United States law.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on patent-publication exchange, action copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks authority for Japan to resume exchanging patent specifications with foreign patent offices.
subfiles.summary: The Civil Property Custodian and mission say Japan can resume the exchange with little administrative burden, but SCAP needs a directive. This is a noisy action copy of the airgram reproduced on pages 253–254.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Designates a white airgram copy as the record copy after the yellow action copy was not returned.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the replacement copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on patent-publication exchange, record copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends authorization for the Japanese Patent Bureau to resume international exchanges of patent specifications.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the Civil Property Custodian's view that exchange can resume with little burden, notes requests from Korea and the United Kingdom, and suggests an interim directive. This is the record copy of the airgram on pages 250–251.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Civil Property Custodian patent report
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a secret report on Japanese patent property and the Patent Property Division's work.
subfiles.summary: Sends two copies of the November 1947 report.

subfiles.title: Comprehensive report of patent property
subfiles.from: Patent Property Division, Civil Property Custodian, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese patent property, royalties, wartime actions, and plans for restitution and publication.
subfiles.summary: Provides counts by ownership and property type, together with patent and copyright royalty totals. Describes secret and Japanese government patents, German holdings, and wartime measures against Allied patents and trademarks. Reviews copyright problems and sets out work on restitution, compensation, infringement, and publication. The final page lists the report's appended orders, memoranda, policy summaries, and legal survey.

subfiles.title: General Order No. 10 establishing the Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP, by command of General MacArthur
subfiles.to: Civil Property Custodian and GHQ staff
subfiles.about: Establishes the Civil Property Custodian and defines its authority over property and assets.
subfiles.summary: Assigns custody, control, preservation, disposition, restitution recommendations, and recordkeeping for Allied, neutral, enemy, and Japanese property.

subfiles.title: Organizational Memorandum No. 1: Patent Branch
subfiles.from: Franklin R. Sibert, Deputy Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Establishes a Patent Branch for patents, utility models, designs, trademarks, and copyrights.
subfiles.summary: Defines duties for preserving rights, gathering records, handling claims, controlling enemy property, and advising on restitution. Assigns the Comptroller responsibility for property accounts and title records.

subfiles.title: Organizational memorandum establishing Patent Division
subfiles.from: Patrick H. Tansey, Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Temporarily establishes a Patent Division under Franklin R. Sibert.
subfiles.summary: Names the division's initial staff and headquarters room.

subfiles.title: Duties and responsibilities of the Patent Property Division
subfiles.from: Patrick H. Tansey, Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Defines the division's responsibilities and four branches.
subfiles.summary: Assigns the division control of Allied, enemy, and Japanese government intellectual property, including secret patents and technical information. Describes the German Patents, Commercial Patents, Trademarks and Copyrights, and Research and Analysis branches.

subfiles.title: Definition of patent property
subfiles.from: Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Defines the property and related rights covered by the Patent Property Division.
subfiles.summary: Includes patents, models, designs, marks, copyrights, applications, technical information, agreements, claims, and revenues.

subfiles.title: Patent Property Division organization chart
subfiles.from: Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Shows the division director and its four branches.
subfiles.summary: Names Major E. G. Schuck as director.

subfiles.title: Japanese Bureau of Patents and Standards organization chart
subfiles.from: Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Charts the Japanese bureau's divisions, sections, and staffing.
subfiles.summary: Names K. Kubo as Director General and lists personnel totals.

subfiles.title: Résumé of SWNCC 369: treatment of Japanese patents
subfiles.from: Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Summarizes proposed policy for Japanese domestic and foreign patents and utility models.
subfiles.summary: Proposes restoration and extension of Allied rights, priority for wartime-blocked applications, compulsory licensing when needed for Japan's economy, publication of secret patents, and royalty accounting. It also addresses former Japanese interests abroad and postwar Japanese inventions.

subfiles.title: Summary of German Patent Accord
subfiles.from: Civil Property Custodian
subfiles.about: Summarizes the London Accord's treatment of former German-owned patents.
subfiles.summary: Explains royalty-free use among participating nations and protection of certain preexisting non-German rights.

subfiles.title: Brief summary of patent laws of Japan
subfiles.from: Civil Property Custodian; based on translations by J. E. DeBecker
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese rules for patents, utility models, designs, trademarks, and copyrights.
subfiles.summary: Reviews patent eligibility, duration, fees, priority, government use, and appeals, then utility-model and design rights. Its longer trademark account covers registration, exclusions, opposition, use, renewal, transfer, and cancellation. The copyright account describes protected works and persons, duration, exclusive rights, restrictions, remedies, agency licensing, and publication or broadcast permissions. The copyright summary continues beyond page 290.
